changes: Your calendar finally shows your own wall-clock time: the account timezone is adopted from your browser on the next visit and can be changed to any zone in Settings
Meeting invites in the mobile apps show the answer you already gave, including replies made on the web
Calendar apps follow your account timezone instead of the device's
A new tagged version is a beta until it is marked stable
Leaving the beta channel offers a reinstall of the latest stable
Admin -> Updates can follow tagged versions before they are marked stable
Subscribe to a public ICS calendar URL as a read-only calendar
Releases are now numbered YYYY.MICRO (this is 2026.29) - a year and one serial, shared with the iOS app
Instances that never installed v2026.08.28 cannot read this update and have to be updated by hand
iCloud calendars and their events keep their real colour instead of falling back to grey - Apple's CalDAV sends the colour with an alpha channel and it was being rejected
The updater accepts the two-component version format, so this instance can still see releases after the numbering changes

The iCloud Reminders list (“Påminnelser ⚠️”) no longer appears as a calendar - reminder collections are filtered out of CalDAV discovery, and vanished calendars without events are cleaned up automatically
Today is marked with a filled date circle in the calendar's week and month views
A birthday that repeats once a year no longer shows up on the same date every month
Calendars with thousands of events now finish their first sync instead of timing out and staying empty
A reminder stored in a calendar no longer blocks every event in that calendar from syncing
iCloud calendars pull their events again - every one of them had been stuck at zero since CalDAV support landed
A calendar whose own sync fails now says so under its name, in the web rail and in the native apps, instead of just looking empty
Calendar invitations show attendee names and their replies in the native apps
Editing or deleting one occurrence of a repeating event now acts on the occurrence you picked, not the first one in the series
Calendar day view is a HEY-style filmstrip: a continuous timeline with color slats and night bands
Drag on the day view to create an event, or drag an event to move it
Week and month events render in solid calendar colors with serif day numerals
List views share the same row, actions, and per-list search
Sent paginates like the other mailboxes
Files open the containing thread in the right folder
Native apps can edit a scheduled send via PATCH
Inbox hover actions now spell out Follow up, Snooze and Archive instead of anonymous F/S/E glyphs
APNs alerts include content-available so the native apps can sync new mail without focusing the window
Reply drafts show the thread sender and subject in Drafts
Opening a reply draft lands on the thread with the composer already open
MCP save_draft requires a real message id and get_thread returns the draft
Large attachments upload in chunks via MCP and the native app. A 1.5 MB PDF no longer has to travel as one base64 payload
Web drafts stay in sync with MCP and Mac. Restored attachments show their real filename and size instead of Attachment 0 B
MCP attachments: PDFs come through as real bytes instead of empty 0-byte files
MCP attachments: PDFs come through as real bytes instead of empty 0-byte files
Settings backup Off / Daily / Weekly stay clickable after you pick a schedule
Settings takeout: contacts, screening, and preferences as a dummy Sent email. Daily or weekly cadence, last 4 copies, restore after a wipe from the same mailbox
Docker image carries the Kamal `service` label so the CI-built ghcr.io image can be deployed directly (no local build); release docs updated
Sending a mail now deletes the draft it came from on the server (web composer and MCP send_mail pass the draft key), so drafts no longer linger in the Drafts list after a successful send
Claude Code now loads Kurir's MCP tools: results include resultType (required by the 2026-07-28 revision) and tools/list uses cacheScope "private" instead of the invalid "server"

Claude Code can now connect to /mcp: server/discover returns supportedVersions and serverInfo in _meta per the 2026-07-28 revision, so clients no longer fall back to legacy initialize and fail with -32600
Connecting Claude Code via /mcp no longer fails with "Invalid redirect" - loopback OAuth redirect URIs are accepted on any port (RFC 8252 §7.3)
Connect Claude to your Kurir instance at /mcp with passkey consent
Agents can read, search, triage, screen senders, and change your own settings
Sending mail and other destructive actions ask for a confirmation in Claude first
Revoke connected apps under Settings → Connected apps
Connect Claude to your Kurir instance at /mcp with passkey consent
Agents can read, search, triage, screen senders, and change your own settings
Sending mail and other destructive actions ask for a confirmation in Claude first
Revoke connected apps under Settings → Connected apps
Closed a hole where any signed-in user could read or create contacts under another account
Rejected mail no longer disappears from the app if the IMAP archive move fails
Undo after screening out a sender now brings the mail back from the archive
Compose no longer sends twice on a double-click
Sending a scheduled message now (or undoing it) no longer loses the copy if you refresh during the undo window
Drafts keep Cc/Bcc and attachments, including files forwarded from IMAP
Tracker images hidden in CSS comments are blocked; the image proxy no longer follows DNS rebinding to internal addresses
Sign-in, register, and other auth pages scroll again when the content is taller than the window (small windows and in-app sign-in sheets clipped the page before)
Demo instances show the demo credentials form first on the sign-in page, with the passkey button below it
Drafts catalog: a labeled Delete button on every row, with a confirmation dialog before the draft is removed
Drafts rows now show Reply / Forward / New, a To: line, and the same relative timestamps as the rest of the lists
Mouse back (and Esc) closes the open mail and returns to the previous conversation, or the list if that was the first one
New Drafts catalog: every draft - new mail, replies, forwards - in one list, at /drafts on the web, in the iOS More tab, and in the macOS sidebar between Scheduled and Sent
Start several new mails in parallel: each compose now autosaves as its own draft instead of overwriting a single shared slot
Reopening a draft now restores its attachments instead of silently dropping them on the next autosave

Self-host compose now wires up the APNs push relay (PUSH_RELAY_URL), fixing iOS push notifications that never worked on self-hosted installs; existing installs need the compose line added or a re-run of the installer
iOS pushes are skipped with a clear warning when no APNs gateway is configured, instead of failing silently as 'relay unreachable'

Mobile sync now includes the user's remote-image policy (imagePolicy) so the iOS/macOS app mirrors the web privacy setting, including the load-images-block-trackers mode with its trackers-blocked badge
Screen domain retroactively: create a domain rule from an existing message (thread header) or screened sender — the sender moves with the rule
Mobile: the createDomainRule action moves the origin sender, enabling Screen domain menus in the iOS/macOS app
Domain screening rules: approve or screen out every sender from a domain (or subdomain wildcard) directly from the screener
New rules retroactively decide matching pending senders and apply automatically to new senders at sync
Manage rules at the top of the screened list — change category or remove; removing keeps past decisions
Mobile: domain-rule actions and sync support for the iOS/macOS app
Fix settings connection actions locking up when a request fails or stalls — errors now show inline and controls recover
Backfill this changelog with all releases since April; updating it is now part of every release
Catch-all domains: treat every address on your own domain as yours — in Screener exclusion, sync-time auto-approve, and the mobile sync payload
Settings: catch-all toggle on the connection card next to alias management
Setup wizard collects aliases and the catch-all setting so they apply from the first sync
Sweep stale pending senders for your own addresses to approved/Imbox — hourly and immediately when aliases, send-as, or catch-all change
Fix fresh self-host installs never getting a database schema — the entrypoint now bootstraps empty databases
Fix the search_vector migration silently failing on every boot since Prisma 7
Fix container healthcheck probing ::1 while the app binds IPv4 — installs could never report healthy
Fix install.sh reporting success for an unhealthy app
Redis eviction policy changed to noeviction — required by BullMQ, eviction could drop queued jobs
Fix installer OS detection on rolling-release distros like Arch
Mobile API for the native iOS client: sync, search, actions, compose/send, and APNs push registration
Mobile full-text search backed by the same FTS index as the web
Message body endpoint returns attachment metadata so clients can list and open attachments
Sharpened editorial redesign across the web client; screener uses category icons
Fix sluggish view switching in the mobile PWA
Fix a UI freeze in the PWA when navigating between views and performing actions
Reply Later now removes threads from Imbox, Feed, and Paper Trail (and badge counts) until the flag is cleared, mirroring snooze
New remote-image privacy mode: load images but block known trackers and invisible spy pixels, with a per-thread blocked-tracker indicator
Fix PWA push notifications silently failing when the VAPID keys drifted apart — the public key is now served at runtime
Archiving from the thread view is now instant
New mail (including login codes) arrives within seconds — IMAP IDLE events are no longer dropped during full syncs and connections start at boot
Remove a faint extra border on undo toasts
Remove initial-circle avatars app-wide
Snooze preserves read state so only unread mail is marked unread on wake
Fix scheduled-message double-send when using Send now within the undo window
Contact groups: organize contacts into named groups
Compose supports multiple recipients in immediate and scheduled sends
Editorial redesign of the reading pane, message list, sidebar, and toasts
PDF previews render inline on iOS via pdfjs

Reply Later: stack messages and work through them in a dedicated focus mode
Spy-tracker blocker strips tracking pixels and proxies remote images
Fix vertical scrolling on mobile accidentally triggering swipe-to-archive
Files library: browse every attachment across your mail with type filters, search, and paging (g+l shortcut)
Mobile attachments open through the native iOS share sheet

Un-thread emails from noisy senders — each message renders as its own row, reversible at any time
Fix iOS swipe-back being swallowed in the PWA
Toasts now sit above the bottom bars so Undo is reachable on mobile
Fix paragraph breaks in the compose markdown preview
Reply composer preserves a custom To address when editing finishes
Email body renders in a Shadow DOM instead of an iframe — no pop-in flash and natural mobile scrolling, same CSS isolation and sanitizer guarantees
Swipe-left snoozes to tomorrow 8 AM with an undo toast
Mobile thread view: the bottom action bar is the single archive/snooze/follow-up surface
Fix stale list data after approving, rejecting, or recategorizing a sender
Reply All with Cc and Bcc support and a new keyboard shortcut (a)

Fix updater env var leaking into app container, breaking NEXTAUTH_URL
Fix updater compose project name mismatch causing port conflict
Fix updater status callback blocked by auth middleware
Fix self-hosted auto-update by moving to a companion sidecar container
Add mobile app install docs for iOS and Android PWA
Contact management with multi-email support, linking, and auto-creation
Complete keyboard shortcuts with vim-style navigation
Attachment forwarding for IMAP-synced messages
Admin dashboard with system health monitoring
Auto-update mechanism with rollback support
Landing page and documentation site
One-command installer script
CalVer release tooling
